summary: Executed the 8-phase Logos/ProtonMail-Bridge repair plan under strict safety constraints (live user data, cross-repo, partially destructive). Phases 1 (freeze+backup), 2 (mbsync.nix config fix, cross-repo commit a8f65ad in ~/.dotfiles, home-manager switch verified), 3 (Labels-mirror redundancy verification), 4 (Labels cleanup -- PARTIAL via documented safety fallback), and 6 (headerless test-message removal from .Sent) completed. Phase 5 (Trash/Archive UID dedup) is BLOCKED by a critical discovery: verified ALL 862 duplicate-UID pairs (860 Trash + 2 Archive) have DIFFERENT Message-Id values between the two files in each pair -- these are 862 distinct, irreplaceable real messages colliding on the same local UID number from the 2026-02-09 import corruption, NOT redundant copies as the plan assumed. Deleting either member of any pair would destroy real mail with zero redundancy. No safe automated resolution exists without a live IMAP verification pass against the Bridge server (out of scope) or an uncertain rename-only workaround that risks creating new server-side duplicates. Phase 3 also found a related, smaller-scale plan-invalidating discovery: 98.4%/99.8%/62.5%/100% of .Labels.Important/.Labels.Letters/.Labels.EuroTrip/.Labels.CrazyTown content has NO copy anywhere else in the tree (this account has no All-Mail-equivalent channel), so bulk deletion there was also skipped via the plan's own documented Abort-criteria fallback (leave inert). Phases 7 (reconcile) and 8 (reindex + lift freeze) were consequently NOT attempted since both depend on Phase 5. email-freeze remains active. No data was lost: all destructive steps stopped before any irreversible action once the underlying assumptions were disproven by direct verification.
blockers: Phase 5 (Trash/Archive UID dedup): all 862 duplicate-UID pairs verified to contain two messages with DIFFERENT Message-Id values -- no redundancy exists to dedup. Requires a follow-up task with live IMAP verification against the Bridge server (or human-reviewed manual resolution for the 2 tractable Archive pairs) before any keep/remove decision can be made safely. Blocks Phase 7 (reconcile) and Phase 8 (reindex + lift freeze).

Phase 4 (Labels-mirror cleanup): 98.4%/99.8%/62.5%/100% of .Labels.Important/.Labels.Letters/.Labels.EuroTrip/.Labels.CrazyTown content has no copy elsewhere in the tree. Left inert per the plan's own Abort-criteria fallback; the ~38,041-file bloat-reclamation goal is not achieved. Lower priority than the Phase 5 blocker since these files are harmless (will not resync, not growing).
decisions_made: Ran an independent Logos-specific backup in Phase 1 (state files + per-folder tarballs + baseline counts under ~/Mail/.logos-backup-20260706/) because email-freeze's own backup only covers ~/Mail/Gmail.
Verified the Phase 2 config fix at three levels (Nix build, home-manager switch, live generated .mbsyncrc content) before considering it done.

Discarded an initial Phase 3 extraction script whose colon-split parsing broke on maildir filenames containing literal colons in the U=NNN:2,FLAGS suffix; rebuilt using NUL-separated grep -Z -H and independently spot-checked both a positive and multiple negative cases before trusting the result.
Verified Phase 5's Message-Id equality across ALL 862 duplicate-UID pairs (not a sample) before drawing any conclusion, given the irreversibility of a wrong deletion decision.

Considered and rejected a blind rename-only workaround for Phase 5 (strip the colliding U=NNN token without server verification) because it risks mbsync re-uploading the renamed file and creating a new server-side duplicate on the next reconcile.
Marked Phase 4 [PARTIAL] and Phase 5 [PARTIAL]/Phase 7-8 [BLOCKED] rather than forcing through destructive steps whose safety could not be established, per the explicit orchestrator safety directive.

Left email-freeze active at the end of this run rather than lifting it, since the Phase 5 corruption remains unresolved and lifting the freeze risks an accidental mbsync -a trigger via notmuch's preNew hook or aerc's $ keybind.
dead_ends: Do not delete either member of any .Trash/.Archive duplicate-UID pair based on flags, filename batch, or any heuristic without live IMAP server verification -- every one of the 862 pairs checked has two genuinely distinct, real messages, not copies.

Do not clear .Trash/.Archive .mbsyncstate/.uidvalidity while the filename-level U=NNN collision is still physically present -- this does not fix the corruption and may cause unpredictable behavior on the next mbsync logos.
Do not bulk-delete or bulk-move .Labels.Important/.Labels.Letters content without a dedicated follow-up task and human review -- 98%+ of it has no other local copy.
Do not trust a colon-split parse of maildir grep -H output -- maildir filenames contain literal colons in the flag suffix (U=NNN:2,FLAGS); use grep -Z (NUL-separated) instead.
Do not run mbsync logos (or /email --logos --sync) until the Phase 5 blocker is resolved by a dedicated follow-up task.
Do not lift email-freeze until the Phase 5 blocker is resolved and Phase 7's reconcile succeeds.
completion_summary: Applied and verified the mbsync.nix config fix (removed logos-labels from Group logos, cross-repo commit in ~/.dotfiles, home-manager switch verified) and removed the confirmed headerless test message from .Sent. Discovered during safety verification that both remaining destructive steps in the plan (Labels-mirror bulk deletion and Trash/Archive UID dedup) rest on invalidated assumptions -- the vast majority of Labels content and 100% of the duplicate-UID pairs are NOT redundant copies but irreplaceable distinct messages -- so both were left untouched per the plan's own safety fallback rather than risk data loss. Recommend spawning a follow-up task for a live IMAP-verified resolution of the Trash/Archive UID collision before the mbsync reconcile can succeed.
